verses.text: Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel had come there to make him king.
Jeroboam son of Nebat was in Egypt, where he had run away from King Solomon. When he heard about this, he came back from Egypt.
The people sent for him, and Jeroboam and all Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam. They said,
"Your father made us work very hard, like a heavy load on our necks. Now make the hard work and the heavy load your father put on us lighter, and we will serve you."
He said to them, "Come back to me in three days." So the people went away.
King Rehoboam asked advice from the older men who had served his father Solomon while he was alive. He asked, "What do you advise me to answer these people?"
They said to him, "If you are kind to these people, please them, and speak good words to them, they will be your servants forever."
But he ignored the advice the older men gave him. Instead he asked advice from the young men who had grown up with him and who served him.
He asked them, "What do you advise? How should we answer these people who said to me, 'Make the load your father put on us lighter'?"

The young men who had grown up with him said, "Tell the people who said to you, 'Your father made our load heavy, but make it lighter for us,' tell them this: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.
My father put a heavy load on you, but I will make it even heavier. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions.'"
So on the third day Jeroboam and all the people came back to Rehoboam, just as the king had said, "Come back to me on the third day."
The king answered them harshly. King Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older men,
and spoke to them the way the young men had advised. He said, "My father made your load heavy, but I will make it heavier. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions."
So the king did not listen to the people. God made this happen, so that the LORD would keep the promise he had spoken through Ahijah from Shiloh to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

When all Israel saw that the king would not listen to them, they answered the king, "What share do we have in David? We have no part in the son of Jesse! Everyone go home, Israel! David, look after your own family now." So all Israel went home.
But Rehoboam still ruled over the Israelites who lived in the towns of Judah.
Then King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was in charge of the forced workers, and the Israelites threw stones at him until he died. King Rehoboam quickly got into his chariot and escaped to Jerusalem.
So Israel has rebelled against David's family to this day.
